title: Best sprite gen
author: invertednz
selftext: This is probably changing all the time but what do you think is best for generating sprite sheets for animation?

comments.author: mike402
comments.body: Ludo.ai does all the work for you. You get the spritesheet ready to import in the game. Plus a bunch of features like the Pose Generator to make things dead simple

comments.author: missEves
comments.body:
nano banana only works for really simple retro sprite sheets

try it on anything more complex and high res and it’s garbage

you need a more robust pipeline than that

comments.author: RelapseCatAddict
comments.body: I use Pixellab AI with Aseprite, it's been able to make some decent sprite sheets for me to use.

comments.author: Spiritual-Bus-9903
comments.body: If you have a good graphics card you can use comfy UI workflows to generate sprite sheets or I have created pixelartgen.com for generating sprite sheets. It's not the best but it does have multiple pov sprite sheet generations. Honestly I would like you to give it a try.

comments.author: dev-on_rocks
comments.body:
I'm actually making something like this rn.
Any features ur looking for specially?

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body: Try my product AutoSprite, I feel that I’m the best on the market (I’ve used them all) - https://www.autosprite.io/ please let me know if you agree and if you have any feedback, thanks !

replies.author: Gigglen0t
replies.body: I have used autosprite pretty heavily and found that loops no matter the prompt just dont work with your sprite sheets. Running loops always have a strong judder the last frame is always too far away from the first frame.

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback, so by design you need to “knock off the last frame” for perfect loop. I want to give you all the frames but the first and last are the same, so you need to remove the last frame or 2.. sorry that’s confusing I need to make it more clear

replies.author: Gigglen0t
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback! I will give it a shot!

comments.author: Quind1
comments.body: In my experience (and I've tried most tools and have been following them since they were released a few years ago), Ludo and PixelLabs are the best in this area. It helps if you have some Photoshop experience, too. Add some manual refinement/polish, and you're good to go.

comments.author: op_app_pewer
comments.body:
Imo dreamforge.ai has the best sprite+animation generation^^

Although I mostly let its agent create code+assets all at once, like this example game from 5 prompts: https://dreamforge.ai/play/0a25d9-create-a-complete-vampire-survivors-style-arena-

comments.author: missEves
comments.body: [playmix.ai/animate](http://playmix.ai/animate) can generate animated 2d sprites for any art style or asset

comments.author: dorianite
comments.body: I just made [https://spritegen.io](https://spritegen.io) and its currently in beta. Would love feedback!
